q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Revenue Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. Today is August 24, 2026. That's **2 days** until the guidance is announced.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** (not actual results) for Q2 FY2027 revenue. This guidance will be issued during the earnings call on August 26.

The current research provides NVIDIA's guidance issued in May 2026:
- **Guidance: $91.0 billion ± 2%** (range: $89.2B to $92.8B)
- Wall Street consensus: ~$91.9 billion

This is the forward guidance that was previously issued. The key question is: what will NVIDIA guide for going forward?

Most likely scenario: NVIDIA will issue new guidance (or reaffirm existing guidance) at the August 26 earnings call. Given:
1. Q1 FY2027 actual revenue was $81.6B, exceeding guidance by ~$2B
2. NVIDIA has a track record of beating guidance
3. Current guidance of $91B ± 2% appears conservative relative to Wall Street expectations
4. The data center market (NVIDIA's dominant segment) remains robust

NVIDIA will likely either:
- **Maintain or slightly raise Q2 guidance** given the strong Q1 beat
- The research suggests "a similar outperformance in Q2 could push revenue towards $95 billion"

The most probable guidance will be in the **$91-95 billion range**, with the central estimate being **$92-93 billion** (modestly above the current $91B guidance but potentially reflecting confidence from the Q1 beat).

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Unexpected macroeconomic deterioration or recession concerns
- Weaker-than-expected data center demand signals
- Supply chain constraints emerging
- Geopolitical restrictions on China sales proving more restrictive than anticipated
- Competitive pressures from AMD or other vendors intensifying
- If NVIDIA becomes more conservative after Q1 beat (less likely)

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Continued strong data center momentum and demand validation
- Q1 beat of ~$2B encouraging management to raise guidance
- AI/ML adoption accelerating beyond expectations
- Customers front-loading orders before potential future restrictions
- Strong cloud provider capex cycles continuing
- Margin expansion allowing for higher revenue targets

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides the most recent guidance: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** (issued May 2026 for Q2 FY2027).

Historical pattern cited in research:
- Q1 FY2027: Actual $81.6B vs guidance ~$79.6B (approximately $2B beat)
- Research suggests similar outperformance could push Q2 toward $95B

No other specific historical base rates are provided in the research.

---

## Reasoning on the range

The forecast range given is $99.5B to $115.5B. This seems **misaligned** with:
- Current guidance: $91.0B ± 2%
- Wall Street consensus: ~$91.9B
- Maximum expected outperformance scenario: ~$95B

However, I must work with the given range. The question asks what NVIDIA will **guide** for (forward guidance), not actual results. There's a small possibility that:
- NVIDIA could guide significantly higher if they're extremely confident
- Market expectations could have shifted since the research was fetched
- There could be announcement of accelerated demand or new products

But given the research shows current guidance at $91B with Wall Street at $91.9B, a guidance in the $99-115B range would represent an **8-27% jump** from current guidance in just 3 months—extremely unlikely without major catalysts.

More realistically, guidance will be **$91-95B**. On the provided scale (which starts at 99.5B), this means the actual guidance will be **below** the stated range. The question's lower bound is "open—values below are possible," so I must forecast accordingly.

Given the constraints:
- Most likely guidance: $92-93B (modest raise from $91B)
- Probability of guidance >$99.5B: <10% (would require exceptional upside surprise)
- Probability of guidance $89.2-95B: ~85%

---

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA will report its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, after market close. [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8)

NVIDIA's guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued in May 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This implies a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Wall Street analysts' average estimate is approximately $91.9 billion, placing it within NVIDIA's guided range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

The guidance assumes no data center compute revenue from China [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027). Gross margin guidance is 74.9% (GAAP) and 75% (non-GAAP), plus or minus 50 basis points [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027). In Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, exceeding its own guidance by about $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). A similar outperformance in Q2 could push revenue towards $95 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
